page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Page number and running head at the top. Catchword at the bottom right. No marginal notes. Faint small fragments at the bottom left are show-through and are left out.

main_text.p: Præfedisse quoque in Senatu, & agenda consultandave propofuisse non dubitè. Ius étiam in tribunali sedentes dixisse, & in crimina inquisivisse, idem Livius decadis iiii libro iiii sub finem, ubi de emissario Annibalis Aristone Tyrio agit, satis manifeste nos docet. Sed domi rempublicám tantum gessisse, non autem foris rem militarem tractasse, & imperia in exercitus habuisse, aut bellorum duces fuisse, arbitror.
main_text.head: Senatus Carthaginensis.
main_text.p: HIs Suffetibus additus fuit Senatus, quem γερουσίαν[?] Aristoteles, γερόντων[?] quoque Polybius nominant, forsan ex eo quòd non nisi ætate graves in eum admitterentur; Livius ufitato Romanis vocabulo Senatum nuncupat. Qui in eo sedebant senatores, & perpetuos fuisse, & ex optimis quibusque ac ætate provectis per suffragia electos, ideò vero simile est, quòd Aristoteles senatum hunc cum senatu Spartano comparat: Et quòd idem isto nomine laudat hanc rempublicam, quòd in eo ἀριστοί[?] fint, qui eam regunt aut administrant. page.notes: Greek words in the first paragraph of the Senatus passage are doubtful: γερουσίαν, γερόντων and ἀριστοί are copied from a small, uneven print. The Roman numerals "iiii" (decadis iiii libro iiii) are copied as printed and may be misread. "dubitè" is read from a worn e-grave. Show-through and stray marks at the bottom left ("qup", "dnb") are not printed text and are left out.
